title: Effect of crystallinity and morphology on the photocatalytic CO 2  reduction activity of MAPbBr 3
content: Photocatalytic CO2 reduction offers a viable route for converting CO2 into value-added products, and metal halide perovskites have attracted sustained attention as photocatalyst candidates. In this study, MAPbBr3 materials with distinct crystallinity, particle size, and morphology are synthesized via a ligand-assisted reprecipitation process and evaluated for CO2 photoreduction under light irradiation. The MAPbBr3 materials are active for the CO2 photoreduction with CO as the primary product. Sample 1, characterized by larger, well-defined particles and higher crystallinity, achieves a CO evolution rate of 14 µmol g−1 h−1, representing a 2.8-fold improvement over Sample 2, which exhibited smaller, more aggregated particles and lower crystallinity. Systematic characterizations indicate that the improved photocatalytic performance is associated with enhanced light absorption, a slightly reduced bandgap, and more favorable charge carrier dynamics in Sample 1.
